findings.title: 2004-05 and 2005-06 PPG achievement incentives are recorded as 'unrecorded' although closed results show both were met
findings.shown: In the incentive_evaluation of both season_close.json files, achievement is `status: unrecorded`, 'benchmark not machine-readable; needs a recorded evaluation'. The benchmarks are 'At least 15.0 points per game while appearing in at least 60 games' ($236,180, 2004-05) and 'At least 17.0 points per game ... at least 60 games' ($252,660, 2005-06). Every season's contract_schedules row keeps bonus_evaluation = 'each season's incentives are evaluated against closed results at the season rollover (docs/ROADMAP.md item 18)', which is the placeholder text, not an evaluation.
findings.expected: 2004-05: 1,618 pts / 76 G = 21.29 PPG, met. 2005-06: 2,260 pts / 82 G = 27.56 PPG, met. Both are decidable from closed regular-season results, as the minutes clause already is. bonus_evaluation should hold the evaluation, per the incentives.py docstring and ROADMAP item 18 ('built').
findings.evidence: Probe scratchpad/audit/wade_stats/incentives_check.py sums Wade's closed regular-season rows from every played note's declared result file. It prints '2004-05 achievement recorded: unrecorded | expected: met (1618 pts / 76 G = 21.29 PPG; need 15.0 in >= 60 G)' and '2005-06 achievement recorded: unrecorded | expected: met (2260 pts / 82 G = 27.56 PPG; need 17.0 in >= 60 G)'. The same totals reconcile with season_close.json wade.regular (points_per_game 21.29 / 27.56, gp 76 / 82).
findings.scope: Two clauses worth $488,860 of Unlikely bonuses; season_close.json for 2004-05 and 2005-06. bonus_evaluation is a placeholder in all three seasons' contract_schedules rows.
findings.probable_source: runtime/incentives.py:66-75 (evaluate_clause) handles only a 'N regular-season minutes' benchmark and the honor words. A points-per-game/games benchmark falls through to 'unrecorded'. No code writes bonus_evaluation: runtime/signing.py:811 sets the placeholder string and nothing replaces it.
findings.fix_hint: Parse 'At least X points per game while appearing in at least N games' in evaluate_clause using regular_minutes' aggregate (pts/gp and gp). Have the rollover write the evaluation into contract_schedules bonus_evaluation, as documented.

verdict.reason: Reproduced independently. The probe verify-wade-stats/v02_ppg.py reads every played regular-season note's declared result_file and sums Wade's box rows. 2004-05: 76 G, 1,618 PTS, 21.29 PPG. 2005-06: 82 G, 2,260 PTS, 27.56 PPG. Both clauses are met (15.0 PPG in at least 60 G, and 17.0 PPG in at least 60 G). Both season_close.json files record achievement as status 'unrecorded', with evidence 'benchmark not machine-readable'. incentives.evaluate_clause only parses a minutes benchmark and honor words (lines 54-66), so a PPG/games benchmark falls through. The module docstring says the rollover records bonus_evaluation, and ROADMAP item 18 says this is built. But grep finds no writer: runtime/signing.py:811 sets the placeholder string and nothing replaces it. All three seasons' Wade rows (2003-04, 2004-05, 2005-06) still hold the placeholder, including 2003-04, whose season_close evaluated every clause.
verdict.fix_location: runtime/incentives.py:evaluate_clause (lines 48-66): parse 'At least X points per game while appearing in at least N games' from regular_minutes' aggregate. season_close.close never rewrites an existing file, so the 2004-05 and 2005-06 season_close.json incentive_evaluation records need a recorded correction. Add a writer for contract_schedules.json bonus_evaluation at the rollover; runtime/signing.py:811 sets the placeholder that nothing replaces.
verdict.scope_confirmed: Two achievement clauses: $236,180 (2004-05) and $252,660 (2005-06). Two season_close.json files. The bonus_evaluation placeholder appears in Wade's row of all three seasons' contract_schedules.json.

The league pages count all of them (write_back.closed_lines matches them), and the 2005-06 season evidence (season_evidence.compute_totals) has Sweetney and Medvedenko.
findings.evidence: Probe scratchpad/audit/completeness/feedback_minutes.py sums each bbr_id's closed regular-season seconds, taking bbr_id from the requests' frozen inputs. Probe feedback_0304.py does the same through write_back.closed_lines, the league pages' matcher. For 2004-05 and 2005-06 both find exactly these 4 players missing. Every other player's minutes match to 0.1 (marbust01 2,372.5 vs 2,372.4 is only a rounding difference). 2003-04 to 2004-05 is clean. Cause: runtime/write_back.py:380 (game_records) reads bbr_ids only from request[side]['players']. Frozen-format requests (every game from 2004-01-22) carry players under request['frozen'][side]['players'][].stat_profile.bbr_id, so game_records returns bbr None for every row (checked: 'Mike Sweetney', 'Stanislav Medvedenko' -> None). runtime/season_close.py:145 then falls back only to the real-roster key (club, name) and the registry name. Both fail for these players: the result names are 'Mike Sweetney', 'Stanislav Medvedenko' and the literal 'allenma01', while the registry names are 'Michael Sweetney', 'Slava Medvedenko' and 'Malik Allen'. The real 2005-06 rosters put Sweetney and Allen on Chicago and Medvedenko on the Lakers, but the simulation has them on NYK, DET and LAL. closed_lines adds the pid-as-bbr and identity_sources fallbacks, which is why the league pages are right.
